description: Context rules for media, news, streaming, and public-content apps.

effect.appProfileImpact: Media apps often expose public content, but an exported provider still needs an explicit public API contract and must not leak subscriptions, history, bookmarks, or cached account state.

Media playback, sharing, notifications, widgets, and cast integrations can legitimately expose services or receivers. AURA keeps them visible for contract review instead of treating them as automatically critical.
Media apps frequently route links into article, player, subscription, or WebView surfaces. Validate URL, host, and content parameters before release.
Media apps commonly use analytics, ads, streaming, and crash SDKs. They are not automatically defects, but privacy disclosures and data-safety declarations should be checked.
For media apps, backup is usually a review item unless subscriptions, private history, identifiers, or auth tokens are in scope.
